paragraphs: Friend, here's what I love about this one. In days when the word of the LORD was rare, He still spoke (1 Samuel 3:1). He called a boy who "did not yet know the LORD," and He kept calling until the boy heard Him (1 Samuel 3:7, 10). The LORD does not go quiet on people just because they're slow to catch on.

Now look at Eli. Samuel ran to him three times, and the third time Eli realized it was the LORD calling (1 Samuel 3:8). So he gave Samuel the words to say: "Speak, LORD, for Your servant is listening." I think that was a humble thing to do. Eli could have kept the boy in his own room, but he pointed him to the One who was actually calling.

And then came the hard part. The message was heavy, and Samuel was afraid to tell it, but when Eli asked, he "did not hide a thing from him" (1 Samuel 3:15, 18). So here's the lesson for you, baker: listen when God speaks through His word, and don't trim the parts that are hard to hear. The LORD was with Samuel, and He let none of Samuel's words fall to the ground (1 Samuel 3:19). That's a good reason to keep your ears open, and your oven door too!
